technical_and_design_decisions: All new stream management features will be implemented as extensions to the existing Spring XD core stream lifecycle and CLI services, avoiding modifications to core framework code to minimize regression risk.

Message bus resource cleanup will reuse the existing Spring Integration message bus resource management APIs to enumerate and delete queues/topics associated with a stream, rather than implementing custom bus-specific logic.

Inline deployment manifest parsing will support standard Spring Boot-compatible YAML and .properties file formats, leveraging Spring's existing PropertySource and PropertyResolver utilities for parsing and merging.

Optional trace and side channel functionality will be built on top of Spring Integration's native wiretap and dynamic channel creation capabilities, as referenced in the specification, to ensure compatibility with existing messaging patterns.

Reference architecture documentation will be delivered as markdown files with embedded YAML stream definitions, hosted in the project's public documentation repository, and will not include automated deployment scripts (only manual runbooks) per the 'first step' scope noted in U5.
The NYC taxi trip sample stream will use existing Spring XD source, processor, and sink modules where possible to minimize custom code development.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD codebase (including stream lifecycle management, CLI, and message bus abstraction layers) is already available, stable, and supports extension via public APIs, so no core framework rework is required for the new features.

The underlying message bus implementations (e.g., RabbitMQ, Kafka) used by Spring XD expose programmatic APIs for enumerating and deleting queues/topics associated with a given stream, which can be called from the stream cleanup logic.
The inline deployment manifest feature will only need to support local file paths provided via the CLI, not remote (e.g., S3, HTTP) manifest sources, per the scope implied in U4.

The wildcard trace property syntax (module.*.trace) will be resolved using standard Spring property placeholder resolution logic, and will apply to all modules in the stream that have an input/output channel.

Reference architectures will be validated only via local test deployments of the sample stream definitions, not production-grade cloud or on-premises deployment testing, per the 'first step' scope noted in U5.

The NYC taxi trip dataset referenced in U8 is publicly accessible via a static HTTP endpoint or downloadable file, and can be ingested into Spring XD via standard source modules without custom data ingestion code.

activities.activity_description: Add lifecycle hooks to the Spring XD stream destroy operation to identify and delete all associated message bus queues/topics (including stale unused resources) tied to the stream's modules, using existing message bus resource management APIs. Includes error handling for failed cleanup operations and unit testing.

Add CLI support for reading deployment properties from a local YAML or .properties file, merging them with any inline deployment properties provided via the CLI, and validating the merged property set before stream deployment/update. Includes unit testing for file parsing and property merging logic.

Implement a new 'stream update' CLI command and corresponding backend service to modify deployment properties of existing deployed or undeployed streams without requiring full stream destruction and recreation. Includes validation of stream existence, property compatibility checks, and state transition handling for deployed streams. Includes unit and integration testing.

Add support for 'module.<name>.trace' and wildcard 'module.*.trace' deployment properties, which configure Spring Integration wiretap on module input/output channels to enable logging/notification for specified modules. Includes property parsing, wiretap configuration application, and integration with existing Spring XD logging systems. Includes unit and integration testing.

Extend the Spring XD stream DSL and module deployment logic to support declaring additional non-primary (side) channels for modules via deployment properties. Side channels are created on the message bus and can be used for tapping, tracking, or custom integrations. Includes channel lifecycle management (creation, cleanup) and integration testing of side channel routing.

activities.activity_name: Spring XD Reference Architecture Documentation Development
activities.activity_description: Create 3 common reference architecture runbooks (real-time analytics, event-driven microservices, batch data processing) for Spring XD POC development. Each runbook includes an architecture overview, sample stream definitions, deployment steps, and use case guidance. Includes validation that all sample streams deploy and run correctly in a local test environment.

activities.activity_name: NYC Taxi Trip Real-Time Analytics Sample Development
activities.activity_description: Build a functional Spring XD stream that ingests the public NYC taxi trip dataset, performs real-time processing (e.g., average fare calculation by zone, long trip detection), and outputs results to a console or dashboard sink. Includes stream configuration, testing with the full DEBS 2015 challenge dataset, and documentation of the sample.

activities.activity_name: Cross-Feature Integration Testing and Bug Fixing
activities.activity_description: Execute end-to-end integration tests across all new features to validate cross-compatibility, identify and fix defects, and ensure no regression in existing Spring XD stream functionality. Includes test case development, defect resolution, and regression testing.
